candidates.name: Endometriosis
support_spans: a subcutaneous mass in the lower-left abdominal region
The mass was accompanied by slight pain that worsened around menstruation
Revealed endometrial glands consisting of a single layer of monomorphous cuboidal cells with an endometrial stroma
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathology results are consistent with endometriosis, particularly the presence of endometrial glands and stroma in the subcutaneous mass.

candidates.name: Abdominal Wall Endometrioma
support_spans: a subcutaneous nodule of approximately 1 cm diameter was present under the hypogastrium
The mass was accompanied by slight pain that worsened around menstruation
candidates.why: The patient's history of myomectomy and cesarean section, combined with the presence of a subcutaneous nodule with endometrial glands and stroma, suggests abdominal wall endometrioma.

candidates.name: Scar Endometriosis

candidates.why: The patient's history of cesarean section and myomectomy, combined with the presence of a subcutaneous nodule with endometrial glands and stroma near the scar, suggests scar endometriosis.

candidates.name: Subcutaneous Endometrioma
support_spans: a subcutaneous nodule of approximately 1 cm diameter was present under the hypogastrium
Ultrasonography: Showed a hybrid echo-mass about 1.1 × 1.0 cm, with an irregular shape, well-defined border, located 3 mm from the body surface in the subcutaneous soft tissue
candidates.why: The presence of a subcutaneous nodule with endometrial glands and stroma on histopathology suggests a subcutaneous endometrioma.

selector.rationale: The presence of a subcutaneous nodule under the hypogastrium with pain worsening around menstruation, along with the nodule's characteristics, supports Abdominal Wall Endometrioma as the most specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Endometriosis
